questions.question_text: Read the unseen passage segment context. According to the text, why did the little traveler choose to rest under the oak tree during the storm?
options: A) The tree had sweet wild fruits
B) Its thick canopy offered dense shelter from heavy rain
C) A stream flowed right next to its roots
D) He wanted to look for a missing compass map
questions.answer: B) Its thick canopy offered dense shelter from heavy rain

questions.question_text: Based on the passage, what specific natural sound frightened the traveler while he was resting under the oak tree?
options: A) The howling of wolves in the distance
B) The sudden, loud clap of thunder echoing through the valley
C) The chirping of crickets getting louder
D) The sound of rushing river water
questions.answer: B) The sudden, loud clap of thunder echoing through the valley

questions.question_text: Choose the word from the passage that means 'a state of extreme fear or panic'.
questions.answer: C) Terror

questions.question_text: Describe the immediate actions the traveler took after the storm finally passed and the sky cleared. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The traveler stepped out from under the oak tree, shook the water off his cloak, checked his belongings for damage, and resumed his journey toward the distant village.

questions.question_text: What lesson or realization did the traveler experience regarding the unpredictability of nature? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The traveler realized that despite careful planning, nature's sudden fury cannot be predicted or controlled. He learned to respect the elements and appreciate the unexpected shelter provided by the sturdy, ancient oak tree.

questions.question_text: How did the traveler's feelings change from the beginning of the storm to its eventual end? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Initially, the traveler felt anxious, vulnerable, and frightened by the intense lightning and roaring thunder. However, as the storm faded and sunlight emerged, his fear turned into profound relief, gratitude, and renewed courage to continue.

sections.section_name: Section B - Writing Skills & Applied Grammar

questions.question_text: Identify the type of sentence: 'Please submit your English assignments before the deadline tomorrow.'
questions.answer: C) Imperative

questions.question_text: Choose the correct abstract noun formed from the word 'brave'.
questions.answer: D) Bravery

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the appropriate pronoun: The students prepared for the annual play by ____, without any teacher's help.
questions.answer: A) themselves

questions.question_text: Select the sentence where the subject and predicate are correctly identified.
options: A) (Subject: The tall green tree) (Predicate: swayed in the wind.)
B) (Subject: Swayed in the wind) (Predicate: the tall green tree.)
C) (Subject: The tall) (Predicate: green tree swayed in the wind.)
D) (Subject: tree swayed) (Predicate: The tall green in the wind.)
questions.answer: A) (Subject: The tall green tree) (Predicate: swayed in the wind.)

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct degree of adjective: Of all the contestants in the race, Rahul proved to be the ____ runner.
questions.answer: C) fastest

questions.question_text: Identify the correct verb tense in the sentence: 'The train had left the station before we reached the platform.'
questions.answer: C) Past Perfect

questions.question_text: Choose the correct article to complete the sentence: My brother is studying at ____ university located in the city center.
questions.answer: A) a

questions.question_text: Transform this direct speech into indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, 'The Earth revolves around the Sun.'
options: A) The teacher told the students that the Earth revolved around the Sun.
B) The teacher said to the students that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
C) The teacher told the students that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
D) The teacher asked the students if the Earth revolved around the Sun.
questions.answer: C) The teacher told the students that the Earth revolves around the Sun.

questions.question_text: Write a short diary entry expressing your feelings after winning the first prize in an inter-school debate competition. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Dear Diary, Today was an unforgettable day! I participated in the inter-school debate competition and won the first prize. My heart pounded during the speech, but I spoke confidently. Holding the shining trophy made all those late-night rehearsals totally worth it. I feel incredibly proud and grateful for everyone's support.

questions.question_text: Write a short descriptive paragraph about your favorite corner in your school library and why you like spending time there. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: My favorite corner in the school library is the small reading nook near the large glass window. It receives warm natural sunlight and overlooks the quiet botanical garden. The shelves there hold classic adventure novels. I love sitting there because it offers perfect silence and completely transports me into magical worlds.

questions.question_text: Read the extract from 'The Raven and the Fox': 'How handsome you are! If your voice is as sweet as your looks...' What was the Fox's real intention behind these flattering words? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Fox did not actually admire the Raven's looks. His real intention was to trick the foolish bird into opening its mouth to sing, thereby dropping the delicious piece of cheese.

questions.question_text: Read the extract from 'What a Bird Thought': 'I thought the world was made of straw...' What stage of the bird's life does this line represent? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: This line represents the bird's infancy when it was newly hatched. Its entire known world was limited to the small, cozy nest built from dry straw by its mother.

questions.question_text: In the story 'A Bottle of Dew', how did the protagonist initially plan to become rich quickly? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The protagonist blindly believed a local legend and spent years trying to collect five liters of morning dew. He planned to take it to a sage who supposedly possessed a magic spell to turn base objects into solid gold.

questions.question_text: Describe the central conflict in 'Rama to the Rescue'. How did Rama's quick thinking save the day? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The conflict arose when the cunning thief tried to escape with the stolen goods. Rama's quick thinking involved setting a clever trap using scattered marbles, which caused the thief to slip, allowing the guards to capture him easily.

questions.question_text: According to the poem 'A Friend's Prayer', what are two specific qualities the speaker asks for in order to be a good friend? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The speaker prays for the ability to listen patiently without constantly interrupting, and the strength to offer genuine comfort and honest guidance when their friend is going through difficult times or making wrong choices.

questions.question_text: In 'The Unlikely Best Friends', how did the initial differences between the two characters eventually become their greatest strength? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Initially, their contrasting habits caused misunderstandings. However, they soon realized that their opposite traits perfectly complemented each other; one's cautious planning balanced the other's impulsive bravery, helping them overcome a dangerous forest challenge together.

questions.question_text: Based on 'The Chair', explain how an ordinary piece of furniture held deep emotional significance for the grandfather. How did the grandchildren finally understand its value? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The old, creaky wooden chair was not just furniture; it held memories of the grandfather's youth and his late wife. Initially, the grandchildren wanted to throw it away because it looked ugly. They finally understood its immense emotional value when their grandfather tearfully shared the story of how he hand-carved it during his wedding year.

questions.question_text: Discuss the core environmental message presented in 'Neem Baba'. Why is the Neem tree referred to as a 'village pharmacy', and what threats does it face today? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The story highlights the urgent need to protect native trees. The Neem tree is called a 'village pharmacy' because almost every part—leaves, bark, and seeds—has powerful medicinal properties used to treat skin diseases and fever. Today, it faces severe threats from rapid deforestation, urban expansion, and a lack of awareness among the younger generation.
